claims.text: Replacing full thermodynamic integration with MLP-based free-energy perturbation will yield accurate phase-stability free-energy differences in Ta-based BCC high-entropy alloys.
Explicit treatment of lattice distortion and magnetic entropy will prevent kinetic phase-separation artifacts.
Standard EAM potentials fail to capture the liquid structure of multicomponent Ta-based refractory alloys.
DFT thermodynamic integration is computationally prohibitive for the target alloy.
Training on ordered-compound elastic moduli and cohesive energies can provide baseline energetics for a disordered Ta-based HEA potential.
Holder means of atomic-radius and electronegativity properties can model local lattice-distortion effects in an atomistic MLP.
Mean-field magnetic entropy based on longitudinal spin fluctuations links temperature-dependent magnetic moments to free energy.
Kinetic phase separation is a known risk at high temperature near melting in the target class of Ta-based BCC HEAs.
Positive Cr-Ta or Cr-Ni mixing enthalpies drive Laves-phase or B2 decomposition.
Cr-Ta binding can promote Cr2Ta Laves-phase precipitation and reduce BCC stability in a refractory HEA.
Local lattice distortion and magnetic-moment fluctuations are the primary mediators of free-energy changes in the target Ta-based alloy.
Standard EAM potentials omit the relevant lattice-distortion and magnetic-fluctuation contributions.

An MLP trained from ordered compounds and structural descriptors can approximate the potential-energy surface of both the disordered solid and liquid sufficiently well for efficient perturbation sampling.
Ignoring magnetic entropy over-stabilizes disordered phases.
Structural descriptors account for elastic-energy reduction through Laves precipitation or BCC stabilization and thereby prevent kinetic phase-separation artifacts.
The proposed method will predict melting temperature and phase-stability boundaries within 5% of experiment or high-fidelity DFT.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by more than 90% relative to full thermodynamic integration.
The method will correctly predict suppression of Cr2Ta Laves precipitation at high temperature where CALPHAD or EAM may predict it erroneously.
Thermodynamic predictions for HEAs can be inaccurate when the underlying thermodynamic databases are incomplete or contain inaccurate phase-stability parameters.
Training primarily on ordered compounds may not extrapolate accurately to a highly disordered alloy, especially its liquid state.

contradictions.description: The proposal describes kinetic phase separation as an artifact that the MLP will avoid, but also concedes that a static MLP may be unable to capture rapid kinetic phase separation and requires the MLP to reproduce that phenomenon as a falsification criterion. This alternately treats phase separation as a spurious prediction and as a real kinetic behavior that must be reproduced.

The claimed efficiency gain is greater than 90% relative to full DFT thermodynamic integration, whereas the falsification threshold tests whether the gain is less than 50% relative to EAM. Changing the cost comparator means the falsification rule does not directly test the stated efficiency claim.

The conditions characterize Cr-Ta interactions as driving Laves decomposition, while the predicted outcome requires suppression of Cr2Ta at high temperature. Temperature could reconcile these statements, but no transition criterion or supporting evidence is supplied.
